name: etaori_ab
label: eta Ori Aa (Aa1 + Aa2, B1 V + B3 V eclipsing pair, 7.988 d)
sources: Wikipedia infobox (read 2026-10-08) and the papers it cites: P 7.98763(22) d, i 87.62 +/- 0.42 deg, e 0.0095 +/- 0.0010, omega 164 +/- 18 deg; masses 10.87 / 10.54 Msun, radii 6.477 / 4.79 Rsun, T_eff 26 600 / 25 950 K (TESS eclipsing-binary analysis); component V magnitudes Aa 4.50, Ab 5.90, Ac 5.65, B 4.95
van Leeuwen 2007 (Hipparcos): parallax 3.34 +/- 1.07 mas -> 300 pc (+140/-70); no Gaia parallax for this bright multiple
De Mey et al. 1996: spectroscopic orbit of the eclipsing pair
notes: Semi-major axis 0.2171 AU from Kepler's law with the masses and period; at 300 pc that is 0.724 mas with the components 0.201 / 0.149 mas across -- all three scale with the 32 % uncertain Hipparcos distance, which the fringe spacing would measure (a in mas against a in AU: a geometric distance).

Anchor V 4.24 = Aa1 + Aa2 (4.50 + 5.90); the tertiary Ac (V 5.65, B3 V, 44 mas away in a 9.4 yr orbit) sits inside any field stop and adds ~21 % third light that dilutes the fringe contrast by (1 - f3)^2 = 0.62 (campaign option third_light_fraction); eta Ori B (V 4.95, 1.7 arcsec) is excluded.
Eccentricity 0.0095 approximated as circular (eclipses at phases 0.25 and 0.75 in this convention; the disks overlap for |rho| < 0.18 mas, about a fifth of the orbit).
node_pa_deg 0 is ASSUMED: the ascending node of this spectroscopic pair has never been measured -- it is what the Pathfinder's nightly fringe orientation would give.
Claret & Bloemen 2011 Spica law for both components; NewEra does not cover 26 000 K.
assumptions: primary.radius_rsun / secondary.radius_rsun (component diameters from radii and distance)
